misconceptions.misconception: Believing high leverage creates free profits without downside risk.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Because underlying stock has a Gamma of exactly zero, stock trading cannot neutralize portfolio Gamma; managers must trade options with non-zero Gamma ([fact-03]).

misconceptions.authorRebuttal: The BSM differential equation invariant proves that positive Gamma comes at the direct expense of negative Theta time decay ($\Theta + 0.5\sigma^2 S^2 \Gamma = r\Pi$), meaning convexity must be continuously paid for via time decay ([fact-04]).

activeRecallQuiz.question: 1) How do option Gamma and Theta interact according to the BSM differential equation? 2) Why did synthetic portfolio insurance exacerbate the 1987 market crash?

coreTakeaways: Higher-order Greeks (Theta, Gamma, Vega, Rho) quantify critical dimensions of option risk beyond simple price sensitivity ([fact-01], [fact-02], [fact-05], [fact-06]).
Making a portfolio Gamma-neutral or Vega-neutral requires trading option contracts because underlying stock has zero Gamma and zero Vega ([fact-03]).

The BSM differential equation establishes that positive Gamma requires paying continuous negative Theta time decay, while unmanaged synthetic portfolio insurance can catalyze market-wide crash feedback loops ([fact-04], [fact-08]).
